text.p: Seitel Inc Monday described a discovery well at Reedy Creek field in northeastern Jones County, Miss., as a significant discovery for the company.

The well, known as the TexStar Petroleum No. 1 Board of Supervisors 16-3, was drilled to a total depth of 15,195 feet and encountered four potentially productive intervals in the Cotton Valley, Upper and Lower Smackover and Norphlet formations between 14,352 feet through 15,095 feet.
A total of 204 feet of net pay has been logged in the four intervals, with no evidence of an oil-water contact in any of the productive zones.
Currently, production testing is being conducted in the Norphlet formation between 15,012 feet and 15,095 feet with "encouraging" results, Seitel said.

Chief Operating Officer Horace A. Calvert said, "This well represents a significant discovery for our company." Seitel has a 43.5 percent working interest with the rest in held by privately owned companies.
An offset well is slated to be drilled to a total depth of 15,900 feet and is expected to start in March as part of a multi-well development program scheduled for this field in 1997, Calvert said.
The Reedy Creek field has produced 14.9 million barrels of oil and 9.17 billion cubic feet of gas to date, primarily from the Lower Tuscaloosa and Cotton Valley.
